newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt wants more Skase chase details.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt wants more Skase chase details.

text.p: The Australian government said on Thursday it required additional information before a decision could be made on whether to continue funds for efforts to recover assets from failed media tycoon Christopher Skase.
Australian attorney-general Daryl Williams said he had requested the information following discussions with bankruptcy trustee Max Donnelly.
"I have asked Mr Donnelly to provide me with further material so that I may fully examine the possibilities for further action," Williams said in a statement.
He said he would not comment further until he had seen the additional material.
"I can assure the public that everything that can reasonably be done to recover assets which should be available for the benefit of Mr Skase's creditors will be done," he said.
The Australian government announced earlier in October it would review a decision to end funding for the attempted recovery of Skase's assets.
Government authorities said they would end the funding after deciding any further efforts to recover the assets would be unlikely to succeed.
The former Labor government spent A$14 million in a failed attempt to extradite Skase from Spain, where he now lives in self-imposed exile.
The failed tycoon declared himself bankrupt in 1991 with personal debts of A$80 million and left Australia for Spain.
Skase is still wanted in Australia on company charges relating to his failed business dealings.
